question.stem: Lines $y=2x+3$ and $y=11-2x$ meet at P. A line through P parallel to the segment from (1,2) to (4,0) meets the y-axis at Y. Let X be the x-intercept of $y=11-2x$. A different line through Y has twice the gradient of XY. It meets $y=11-2x$ at Z. Find Z's x-coordinate.

options.errorPath: Keep original XY gradient, returning X.
Use the height of P (7) as the y-intercept Y. This gives final slope −28/11 and the intersection equation (2−28/11)x=4.
Use half the original gradient −25/33 rather than twice, so 88=41x.
Use the correct doubled slope −100/33 but draw the final line through the origin. Then (2−100/33)x=11.

workedSolutionSteps: P=(2,7); parallel through P y=−2x/3+25/3, hence Y=(0,25/3). X=(11/2,0), so XY gradient−50/33.

correction.independentCheck: P=(2,7), Y=(0,25/3), X=(11/2,0). With slope −100/33 and intercept 25/3 the intersection satisfies −34x=88, giving choice E. Three negative choices now require distinguishing their magnitudes. Wrong C gives −22/3; wrong F gives −363/34. No added prerequisite.
correction.academicDifficultyAssessment: The repaired version supports a broad Grade 7+ editorial target for linking a gradient, two equations, and successive intersections. Compare November 2018 2H Q18. Finer grade and classroom coverage remain open.
